chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Hajj on behalf of another, does that suffice him from the Hajj of Islam? He said: Yes. I said: Is the Hajj of the camelier (one who leads the caravan) complete or deficient? He said: Complete. I said: Is the Hajj of the hired one complete or deficient? He said: Complete.

key_terms.حَجَّ عَنْ غَيْرِهِ: Hajj performed on behalf of another
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْأَجِيرِ: The Hajj of the hired agent
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْجَمَّالِ: The Hajj of the camelier (contextual proxy type)

ai.seo_question: Does Hajj performed on behalf of another person count as the obligatory Hajj, and is it considered complete?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of Hajj al-Tafwid (proxy Hajj) for fulfilling the primary obligation of Hajj al-Islam, affirming that the performance is complete regardless of whether the agent is a 'camelier' (a term often associated with specific proxy roles or potentially a variant reading for 'mutamatti' or general agent) or a hired agent. It underscores the Shia juristic consensus that the spiritual and legal sufficiency of the ritual rests on the agent's proper execution, thereby validating the practice of delegating the pilgrimage for those unable to perform it themselves.
